nearest_analogues.name: Dashboard-only analytics without an irreversible state change
differences: Candidate targets VC diligence, not generic analytics monitoring.
Demo has node removal changing a counterfactual memo plus saved human override, not a static dashboard.

nearest_analogues.name: Generic chatbot wrapper over a sponsor API
differences: Candidate requires a temporal evidence graph with provenance and constraint checks.
Last-mile output is an auditable partner briefing, not a chat answer.

nearest_analogues.name: rapid-site-builder
differences: Public project builds and ships websites from a prompt; candidate evaluates startup investment evidence.
No shared diligence data model, counterfactual graph, or invest/pass workflow.

observable_differentiator: Time-ordered conviction graph where removing one sourced evidence node changes uncertainty, counterfactual trajectory, top memo risk, and logs a human override.
notes: Nearest supplied analogues are generic and do not share user, problem, data, action, or demo. Main risk is sounding like an AI VC memo; the demo must foreground provenance-linked counterfactual sensitivity.

nearest_analogues.name: Document / PDF summariser
differences: Candidate performs deterministic program-rule math and assertion-level verification, not summary generation.
Applicant correction, deletion state, abstention queue, and human-review export are visible workflow steps.

nearest_analogues.name: Resume / LinkedIn optimiser
differences: Candidate handles affordable-housing documentation under a no-eligibility-decision boundary.
Output is a consented evidence packet with source boxes and audit log, not optimized prose.

nearest_analogues.name: Symptom checker / triage chatbot
differences: Candidate explicitly avoids approval, denial, ranking, scoring, or eligibility triage.
Demo centers document coordinates, stale evidence, OCR correction, and packet-readiness state.

observable_differentiator: Unsupported readiness claims are struck from the export until source-box evidence, effective-date rules, deterministic calculations, and applicant confirmation align.
notes: Crowded around document extraction and checklist assistants, but the no-decision boundary plus deletion/correction audit trail is a meaningful workflow difference if implemented visibly.

nearest_analogues.name: Bounded Outreach Scheduler
differences: Concept-004 classifies facilities as data-gap, no-call, or access-gap candidates; the scheduler creates owner/due-date verification tasks.
Concept-004 cites ADnocap facility data, while the scheduler cites HerLog despite describing facility records.

nearest_analogues.name: Dashboard-only analytics without an irreversible state change
differences: Candidate persists reviewer overrides and changes future shortlist ranking.
It distinguishes missing evidence from true access gaps instead of merely displaying filters.

nearest_analogues.name: Symptom checker / triage chatbot
differences: Facility-planning evidence triage is not patient symptom triage.
Demo uses sparse facility records, source URLs, no-call rules, and reviewer memory.

observable_differentiator: Reviewer can no-call or override a facility classification, save the reason, and immediately change the follow-up shortlist based on evidence-gap memory.
notes: Close internal collision with the outreach scheduler on user, problem, and demo setting. Keep only if positioned as evidence classification memory rather than next-action scheduling.

nearest_analogues.name: Facility Evidence Triage Memory
differences: Scheduler's last-mile action is a concrete call/document/map/supervisor task with owner and due date.
Its cited data source appears inconsistent with the Indian facility workflow, weakening differentiation.

nearest_analogues.name: Dashboard-only analytics without an irreversible state change
differences: Candidate schedules a bounded verification action rather than stopping at a dashboard shortlist.
Shows projected uncertainty reduction from the scheduled action.

nearest_analogues.name: Recommendation list with no last-mile action
differences: Candidate includes owner, due date, action type, and persisted source-backed reason.
Demo has a state transition from facility record to scheduled follow-up task.

observable_differentiator: A ranked facility queue creates one bounded verification task and shows an expected confidence delta for that facility.
notes: Despite a real last-mile scheduling difference, it overlaps heavily with concept-004 on user, problem, sparse facility evidence, uncertainty, provenance, persistence, and demo. The track and data-source metadata are also internally inconsistent, so it should be killed or merged into concept-004 as the action layer.

nearest_analogues.name: VoiceApp.co
differences: VoiceApp is live call coaching for bills/charges; candidate is post-call quote-path scheduling from multiple transcripts.
Candidate adds evidence-linked honesty blocking before calendar action creation.

nearest_analogues.name: NegotiAI
differences: NegotiAI covers prep, live coaching, scripts, records and follow-up; candidate narrows to normalized quote terms and expiry-driven next action.
Candidate's audit trail requires transcript-line support for each scheduled action.

nearest_analogues.name: AI follow-up / meeting transcript tools
differences: Sales tools draft CRM follow-ups from meeting transcripts; candidate targets household vendor quotes and refusal-safe negotiation.
Candidate's core demo blocks unsupported leverage claims, not just generating next steps.

observable_differentiator: A scheduled callback/reminder cannot be created unless the target term, expiry, script, and rationale are tied to exact transcript evidence and pass honesty constraints.
notes: Crowded around negotiation coaching and transcript follow-up, but the post-call quote ledger plus compliance-gated scheduling is a visible workflow difference.

nearest_analogues.name: LeaseStract
differences: LeaseStract abstracts commercial leases with citations; candidate handles affordable-housing packet readiness with program-year boundaries.
Candidate blocks eligibility-style UI transitions rather than exporting an abstract.

nearest_analogues.name: Lease Abstractor AI
differences: Lease Abstractor AI extracts lease fields into Excel; candidate produces neutral applicant receipts from pay stubs and benefit letters.
Candidate's decisive action is a safety interlock, not document extraction.

nearest_analogues.name: Document / PDF summariser
differences: Candidate adds deterministic rule traces and source boxes beyond summary.
Candidate prevents approval, denial, score, rank, or eligibility language from entering the applicant-facing flow.

observable_differentiator: Clicking an unsafe eligibility-result transition is blocked and replaced by an evidence receipt with source boxes, rule version, blocked phrase, and allowed neutral next action.
notes: Document extraction with citations is common, but the applicant-facing safety interlock is materially different if demonstrated as an enforced transition guard.

nearest_analogues.name: MLflow Regression Testing and CI/CD
differences: MLflow provides general pytest-style GenAI regression testing; candidate generates healthcare-facility edge cases from sparse facility rows.
Candidate adds facility-specific no-call/access-gap invariants and failing-row receipts.

nearest_analogues.name: Databricks Evaluate and Monitor AI Agents
differences: Databricks/MLflow already covers evaluation, tracing, monitoring, and quality regression; candidate packages this for a hackathon facility-classifier demo.
Candidate's observable delta is domain-specific release blocking on sparse-field evidence rules.

nearest_analogues.name: Dashboard-only analytics without an irreversible state change
differences: Candidate is not only a dashboard; it creates executable tests and blocks release status.
Candidate shows seeded regression failure and rerun after rule fix.

observable_differentiator: A generated pytest/MLflow suite catches a seeded sparse-field classifier regression and blocks release until the no-call invariant passes on the same fixture.
notes: Core regression-testing mechanism is heavily supplied by MLflow/Databricks; novelty depends on facility-specific invariant generation and judge-facing failure receipts.

nearest_analogues.name: VentureScope
differences: VentureScope verifies claims, benchmarks deals, scores and exports memos; candidate forces scarce analyst-hour and check-review reallocation.
Candidate optimizes value of information instead of primarily producing a company score/recommendation.

nearest_analogues.name: DcernX
differences: DcernX offers structured intake, agentic diligence, IC memos, and decision records; candidate's demo must show actual budget movement between startups.
Candidate frames uncertainty reduction as the allocation objective.

nearest_analogues.name: Kaptrix
differences: Kaptrix already provides evidence lineage, risk registers, confidence audit trails, IC memos, and action plans.
Candidate's distinguishable artifact is a constrained allocator for the next four analyst-hours and provisional check-review slot.

observable_differentiator: The demo visibly moves finite diligence hours and a provisional check-review slot between startups when contradictory evidence changes modeled value of information.
notes: The VC AI diligence space is very crowded with evidence-backed memo, scoring, contradiction, and audit-trail tools. Keep only if the allocator is central and executable, not an extra visualization on a standard diligence memo.

nearest_analogues.name: NegotiAI
differences: NegotiAI provides live coaching, scripts, outcome records and follow-up actions; candidate opens a minimal conflict review task after conflicting calls.
Candidate compresses review scope to disputed transcript spans and unresolved quote terms.

nearest_analogues.name: VoiceApp.co
differences: VoiceApp coaches live consumer disputes; candidate performs post-call contradiction minimization across vendors.
Candidate sends only the smallest evidence set to a reviewer or household co-decision-maker.

nearest_analogues.name: Document / PDF summariser
differences: Candidate is not a summary of full transcripts; it computes a minimal conflict set.
Candidate distinguishes unsupported leverage, refused line items, changed terms, and callback questions.

observable_differentiator: A 42-line transcript bundle becomes a four-span review task that preserves price-changing conflicts while excluding irrelevant transcript text.
notes: Close to consumer negotiation assistants and transcript-analysis tools, but minimal-conflict task opening is a clear last-mile action if evaluated against recall of true price-changing conflicts.

nearest_analogues.name: Databricks Unity Catalog Lineage
differences: Unity Catalog tracks table, column, job, notebook, and dashboard lineage; candidate tracks claim-level facility assertions and reviewer decisions.
Candidate changes a public-health planning shortlist based on provenance states.

nearest_analogues.name: Indian Public Health Standards dashboard
differences: IPHS is an official facility assessment/dashboard system; candidate is a hackathon Databricks ledger for sparse-row provenance and shortlist changes.
Candidate preserves accept/reject/revise/override events at assertion level.

nearest_analogues.name: Dashboard-only analytics without an irreversible state change
differences: Candidate commits planner actions to a persistent ledger instead of only filtering/map display.
Candidate blocks unsupported capacity claims from entering the retained shortlist.

observable_differentiator: Planner accept, reject, revise, and override events update an append-only claim provenance ledger and reduce the shortlist from unsupported candidates to verified review-ready facilities.
notes: Data lineage and facility dashboards already exist, but combining claim-level provenance with planner state transitions is distinct enough if the ledger drives the shortlist rather than annotating it.
